newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt slows, Russia lower on Chubais comments.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt slows, Russia lower on Chubais comments.

text.p: Trading of emerging market debt slowed sharply in Europe on Wednesday as players waited for more U.S. data.
International trade data and the Philadelphia Fed survey due later will be closely watched for indications of inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy.
"Overall it is very quiet, although Russian debt is a touch softer," a debt trader at a U.S. bank said.
"There are virtually no trades taking place."
Russian dollar Vnesh bonds were trading at 76.875/77.375 cents, down a quarter of a point.
"Prices have eased a bit from overnight levels, but the focus is still on U.S. Treasuries," John Bunner, deputy director of asset trading at Moscow Narodny said.
"Chubais's comments about the budget were a bit unnerving. But the market generally is subdued and rather pessimistic as it waits for further data," he said.

Earlier, Russian finance minister Anatoly Chubais told the upper house of parliament that the 1997 budget was unrealistic and promised to cut spending and raised over $5.0 billion through state sell-offs and precious metal sales.
Looking ahead, traders said emerging debt would continue to track the U.S. Treasury market.
"Until we see a much clearer direction in interest rate expectations, the Brady market will continue like it is now," Bunner said. -- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
